clues: Some groundwater animals here have survived environmental changes extending back through the Ice Age.
Eruptions beneath ice can release sudden floods known as jökulhlaups.
Those floods help reshape outwash plains, rivers and rapidly changing canyons.
Several central volcanoes lie beneath the great ice cap at the heart of this protected area.
In south-eastern Iceland, find the national park where a vast ice cap and active volcanism meet.
targetLabel: Vatnajökull National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: This landscape makes the interaction of ice, eruptions and flowing water visible. A jökulhlaup is a sudden glacial outburst flood, and the source describes eruption-related examples here; the clue does not claim that every such flood everywhere has the same cause. The point represents the designated park.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
